decisions.what: Implement the three /api/chatbot stubs as zero-parameter sync GET/POST handlers returning NextResponse.json({ error: 'chatbot endpoints retired' }, { status: 501 }).
decisions.why: A parameterless signature makes 'input is never read' a compile-time guarantee — TypeScript rejects passing a Request, so no auth/body/query dependency can silently return.
rejected: (req: Request) signature kept for symmetry with old handlers — weaker guarantee, invites body/auth reuse
shared stub helper across the three routes — design §9 locks intentional duplication for simpler future deletion

decisions.what: Replace the deleted chatbot route test wholesale with a fresh 501-contract test file at the same path (11 tests), instead of editing the old 1884-line test in place.
decisions.why: The old file imported deleted modules and asserted the retired 200/401/400 contract; a clean rewrite locks the new unconditional-501 contract with zero stale mocks.
rejected: incremental edit of the old route.test.ts — would drag dead vi.mock config for deleted modules
e2e curl-based verification — deferred to substrate-cutover's post-migration checklist

blockers.what: developer subagent cd'd to the repo root, so its first edit/stage pass landed in the main checkout instead of the worktree; the commit-guard hook (worktree lacked node_modules) blocked the commit.
blockers.resolution: moved work via git stash push -u in the main checkout, stash pop in the worktree, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile there; verified main checkout restored clean and stash empty

blockers.what: transient 'connection refused' to api.github.com broke auto-extract.sh's gh pr view during /log-episode
blockers.resolution: retried after ~10 s; single network blip

learnings: In worktree sessions, brief subagents with the absolute worktree path: a bare cd to the repo root silently edits the main checkout.
Zero-parameter route handlers turn 'request is ignored' into a compile-time property — stronger and cheaper than runtime input-matrix tests.
An independent re-review on a different model (Fable) reproduced the first verdict and per-AC evidence — cheap cross-model confirmation for destructive chores.
Test scenarios drafted from historical patterns can drift from as-built signatures; verify with LSP before writing tests.
